$comment: France, Civil Law (Responsabilite civile) - THE FIRST POPULATED AUTHORITY GRAPH ENTRY FOR FRANCE. Article 1240 Code civil's general fault-based extracontractual liability provision, and the Assemblee pleniere's construction of 'faute' as an objective standard not requiring the actor's subjective capacity to understand the consequences of their conduct - applied here to a 5-year-old child. Both nodes fetched cleanly from Legifrance with no access issues, a clean counterpoint to the access difficulties encountered in Spain's research passes.
verification_method: Code civil art.1240 fetched live and directly from legifrance.gouv.fr, independently re-fetched and word-for-word consistent on both attempts. Cass., Assemblee pleniere, 9 mai 1984 (arret Derguini), n.80-93.481 fetched live and directly from legifrance.gouv.fr's jurisprudence database, independently re-fetched and word-for-word consistent on the holding quote.

authorities.name: Code civil, article 1240
authorities.citation: Code civil, art.1240 (formerly art.1382, renumbered without substantive change by Ordonnance n.2016-131 of 10 February 2016)
authorities.date_note: Date the renumbering to art.1240 took effect. The provision's substance dates to the original 1804 Code civil (as art.1382); the text verified this session is the current in-force version.
authorities.proposition: Tout fait quelconque de l'homme, qui cause a autrui un dommage, oblige celui par la faute duquel il est arrive a le reparer. [English: any human act whatsoever that causes damage to another obliges the person by whose fault it occurred to make reparation for it - France's general, catch-all provision of extracontractual liability, requiring only fault (faute), damage (dommage), and a causal link (lien de causalite) between them.]
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, on two independent passes, word-for-word consistent both times.

authorities.name: Arret Derguini
authorities.citation: Cass., Assemblee pleniere, 9 mai 1984, n.80-93.481, Publie au bulletin
authorities.judge_or_panel: Assemblee pleniere (the Cour de cassation's highest formation, empowered to resolve conflicts between lower courts and set doctrine)
authorities.proposition: Construes the 'faute' element of art.1382 (now art.1240) objectively: liability for fault does not depend on the actor's subjective capacity to understand or foresee the consequences of their conduct. A 5-year-old child, struck by a car while crossing at a protected pedestrian crossing, was found to have committed a fault contributing to her own injury even though she lacked the capacity to discern (discernement) the consequences of her acts - 'la Cour d'appel, qui n'etait pas tenue de verifier si la mineure etait capable de discerner les consequences de tels actes, a pu, sans se contredire, retenir, sur le fondement de l'article 1382 du Code civil, que la victime avait commis une faute qui avait concouru... a la realisation du dommage.' [English: the Court of Appeal was not required to verify whether the minor was capable of discerning the consequences of her acts before finding, under article 1382, that she had committed a fault.] This ruling, alongside a companion decision the same day (arret Lemaire, not independently verified in this file) and later extended to the mentally incapacitated (arret Fullenwarth, Ass. plen., 9 mai 1984, not independently verified in this file), remains the foundational authority for the objective standard of fault under French delictual liability.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from legifrance.gouv.fr's jurisprudence database this session, independently re-fetched - both fetches word-for-word consistent on the holding quote. No ECLI identifier is displayed on the Legifrance record for this pre-ECLI-era 1984 judgment, consistent with that era's citation practice rather than an omission. The case's identity, formation, and doctrinal significance were also cross-checked against two independent secondary sources (legavox.fr, fiches-droit.com), both agreeing on the same date, formation, pourvoi number, and holding, though neither reproduces the verbatim attendu.

edges.verified_via: Arret Derguini, Cass. Ass. plen., 9 mai 1984, fetched directly from legifrance.gouv.fr's jurisprudence database and independently re-confirmed: construes art.1382/1240's fault requirement as an objective standard, not dependent on the actor's subjective capacity for discernement.

what_this_is_not: Two nodes covering the objective fault standard under France's general extracontractual liability provision - France's first-ever populated Authority Graph entry in this repository. Does not cover the causation or damage elements in detail, vicarious/parental liability under art.1242, or any other French Civil Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
